record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine the smallest possible maximum degree that always suffices to construct a plane spanner on an arbitrary finite planar point set.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 14. What is the smallest maximum degree that can be achieved for plane spanners?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of points in the plane, a geometric graph on $P$ is a graph whose vertex set is $P$ and whose edges are straight-line segments between pairs of points of $P$, with edge weights equal to the Euclidean lengths of the segments. Such a graph is called plane if no two of its edges cross. For a real number $t\geq 1$, a geometric graph $G$ on $P$ is a $t$-spanner of $P$ if for every pair $p,q\in P$ the length of a shortest path from $p$ to $q$ in $G$ is at most $t\cdot\|p-q\|$. The maximum degree of $G$ is $\Delta(G)=\max_{v\in P}\deg_G(v)$.

Determine the smallest integer $\Delta^\ast$ with the following property: there exists a constant $t\geq 1$ (independent of $P$) such that for every finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ there exists a plane $t$-spanner $G$ on $P$ with $\Delta(G)\leq \Delta^\ast$.
artifact.status_search_result: It is known that 3 is a lower bound on the maximum degree of any plane spanner. Bonichon, Kanj, Perković, and Ravelomanana (2014) proved that maximum degree 4 always suffices, with stretch factor improved by Kanj, Perković, and Türkoğlu (SoCG 2016) to 20. Whether maximum degree 3 suffices for arbitrary point sets remains open; for points in convex position degree 3 is known to be tight.

status_evidence.title: There are Plane Spanners of Maximum Degree 4
status_evidence.snippet: The complete Euclidean graph always contains a plane spanner of maximum degree at most 4.
status_evidence.claim: Maximum degree 4 is achievable for plane spanners on any point set.

status_evidence.title: Degree Four Plane Spanners: Simpler and Better
status_evidence.snippet: Plane spanner of maximum degree at most 4 and stretch factor at most 20; the lower bound on the degree of any plane spanner is 3.
status_evidence.claim: Best upper bound is 4; lower bound is 3; gap remains open.
